history.period: One weak source claims the original structure dates to 1699 (verify - single source, rebuilt several times since)
history.summary: The Khandoba Temple is a small, well-maintained shrine on the Nagar-Manmad (Ahmednagar-Kopargaon) Road, about 300 m from the Shirdi bus stand. It is pivotal to Sai Baba's story: when Baba returned to Shirdi with Chand Bhai's wedding party, he rested under the banyan tree near the temple, where the priest Mhalsapati greeted him with 'Aao Sai' ('welcome, Sai') - the origin of the name 'Sai'. Baba first chose the temple as his residence, but Mhalsapati, taking him for a Muslim, refused; Baba then settled in the dilapidated Dwarkamai mosque. The temple holds an ancient stone idol of Khandoba with his consorts Mhalsa and Banai, a separate shrine for his horse Shyamsundar, and a shrine with Sai Baba's idol and padukas. A rectangular sandpit/Agnikund in front was traditionally used for fire-walking on Champa Shashti. A grand annual palanquin procession starts from the temple commemorating the event when Baba warded off cholera by marking Shirdi's borders with wheat flour.

name: Khandoba Temple
town_description: Shirdi is a pilgrimage town in Rahata taluka of Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra, about 83 km from Ahmednagar and 307 km from Mumbai. Built around the life and samadhi of Sai Baba, it is one of India's busiest pilgrimage centres, attracting tens of millions of devotees of all faiths every year. The Khandoba Temple lies on the town's main approach road, a few hundred metres from the Samadhi Mandir.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism - Khandoba as a form of Shiva)
